definition_quote.value: Optometry means the art and science of visual care and is declared to be a learned profession. The practice of optometry consists of the diagnosis and interpretation of the visual behavior of the human organism by the employment of any means other than surgery. The practice of optometry further consists of the correction of visual anomalies through the prescribing, employment, and use of lenses, prisms, frames, mountings, contact lenses, orthoptic exercises, and visual training, light frequencies, and any other means or methods for the relief, correction, or remedy of any insufficiencies or abnormal conditions of the human visual organism, other than surgery.

drug_authority.value: Certified optometrists may use pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic and treatment purposes. Treatment agents are limited to nonnarcotic oral analgesics, hydrocodone (oral, up to 48 hours), Schedule III or IV oral analgesics for ocular pain (up to 72 hours), and other agents for ocular disease (excluding Schedule I or II controlled substances). May administer by injection (with restrictions on specific injection types). May not dispense pharmaceutical agents. May not treat systemic diseases.
drug_authority.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit the use, administration, or prescription of pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic purposes and treatment of ocular disease in the practice of optometry by optometrists who have received pharmacological training and certification from a properly accredited institution of higher learning and who are certified by the board to use pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic and treatment purposes.
